description:
Produce the design study that fixes the additive-NTT implementation approach: basis choice, tower-field integration, API placement, and benchmark methodology.

## Background

The additive NTT evaluates polynomials over an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear subspace in $O(n \log n)$ field operations using the novel polynomial basis [Lch2014]. Implementations differ in basis convention (Cantor basis versus the novel basis as used by binary-tower proof systems [DiamondPosen2023]), in how twiddle-like constants are precomputed, and in how the transform composes with tower-field arithmetic. These choices are hard to reverse after kernels are written, so they are fixed in a design study before implementation.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A design document selects the polynomial basis and subspace convention with rationale, including compatibility with the existing GF($2^m$) and tower-extension representations.
- [hard] REQ-02: The document specifies the API surface (crate placement, types, precomputation lifecycle) and at least four placement options are weighed before the recommendation.
- [hard] REQ-03: The document defines the benchmark methodology for the crossover-versus-Karatsuba measurement and the external-baseline comparison, naming datasets, sizes, and metrics.
- [hard] REQ-04: Open risks (numerical conventions, licensing of comparison baselines, SIMD portability) are enumerated with mitigations.

## References

- [Lch2014] Lin, Chung, Han — Novel Polynomial Basis and Its Application to Reed–Solomon Erasure Codes. FOCS 2014. arXiv:1404.3458.
- [DiamondPosen2023] Diamond, Posen — Succinct Arguments over Towers of Binary Fields (Binius). IACR eprint 2023/1784; EUROCRYPT 2025.
title: Design study for the additive NTT: basis, tower integration, API, benchmarks
